{{recipesummary|category=Pasta recipes|servings=4|time=30 minutes|difficulty=1|image=[[File:Spaghetti served with meat sauce.jpg|300px]]}}
{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Cuisine of Italy]] | [[Cookbook:Italian-American cuisine|Italian-American cuisine]]

== Ingredients ==
For 4 servings:
* 2.25 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]] (10 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) water
* 8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] (224 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Spaghetti|spaghetti]]
* 2.5 cups (24 oz) pasta sauce (optional but recommended)
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] (optional but recommended)
* [[Cookbook:Vegetable Oil|Vegetable oil]] (optional but recommended)

== Procedure ==

# On a stovetop, bring the water to a boil on high heat after adding salt and vegetable oil (see tips below).
# Reduce heat to medium and add the pasta.
# While the spaghetti is cooking, pour desired amount of sauce into pan and set stove to medium.
# Set a timer for 7 minutes. When the timer goes off, fish out a strand of spaghetti and bite into it.  What you're going for here is al dente, meaning that the pasta is just soft enough to eat: no longer crunchy in the middle, and not mushy and over-done. A more traditional (but messy) way to see if the spaghetti is done is to throw some strands onto a wall.  If they stick to the wall, then the pasta is ready to eat.
# When the sauce begins to bubble, reduce the heat to its lowest setting and cover. 
# Once the pasta is ready, carefully drain it through a colander into a sink. 
# Serve sauce over pasta in bowls.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Adding salt to the cooking water enhances the pasta flavor and to allows the water to boil more quickly. Adding vegetable oil to the cooking water helps prevent the spaghetti from sticking together.
* Try adding herbs or fruit (such as [[Cookbook:Pineapple|pineapple]] tidbits) to the water before it boils to keep with the pasta after straining for extra flavor and texture.
* Before cooking the sauce, consider [[Cookbook:sauté|sauté]]ing some finely minced onions, [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], ground [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] (or [[Cookbook:Pork|pork]]/[[Cookbook:Sausage|sausage]]/[[Cookbook:Veal|veal]]/etc.), cheese ([[Cookbook:Parmesan Cheese|parmesan]]/[[Cookbook:Mozzarella Cheese|mozzarella]]/etc.), [[Cookbook:Mushroom|mushrooms]], or anything else that catches your fancy. Then add the sauce. 
* In a pinch, you can make plain spaghetti and add ketchup if you do not have any pasta sauce available.
* The following foods go well with spaghetti and can be served together:
** [[Cookbook:Broccoli|Broccoli]] (or other [[Cookbook:Vegetable|vegetables]]).
** [[Cookbook:Garlic Bread|Garlic Bread]]
** [[Cookbook:Meatballs|Meatballs]]
** [[Cookbook:Pineapple|Pineapple]] (or other [[Cookbook:Fruit|fruits]]) tidbits ([[Cookbook:Boiling|boiled]], [[Cookbook:Grilling|grilled]], or [[Cookbook:Frying|fried]])
** Shredded and/or grated [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]]
** [[Cookbook:Tomato Sauce|Tomato]], [[Cookbook:Alfredo Sauce|alfredo]], or other [[Cookbook:Sauces|sauces]] (can choose one, the other, or mixed together)
* Cooking is about experimentation—never be afraid to try anything once!
